passages.text: 2026-08-02 **2026-08-02, third maintenance pass (unattended) — one target row, and two tools the pass was refused.** Ingest captured 0 new items across all six channels for the second pass running, so this pass worked the backlog. **Target: "The agent has to guess what resources it's actually working with"** — chosen because it carries no evidence-debt gate, was not among the eight gated rows named this morning, sits top-level under the Outcome (it conditions planning on every branch rather than one), and its own body already names distinct mechanisms with real trade-offs, so the litmus test was passed before this pass touched it. Three candidate solutions with deliberately different failure modes — declaration ("A declared resource manifest the planner must cite before it ranks anything"), inference-from-failure ("Constraint profile mined from what actually blocked the loop"), and periodic elicitation with decay ("Expiring resource questions asked at a fixed cadence") — each with one assumption test carrying a pre-committed threshold in the `threshold` field, spread across value, feasibility, and viability. `solutionsMissingAssumptions` stays at zero. **Held: the remaining 18 rows**, for the reasons already recorded in the two ledgers above — eight carry an explicit gate in their own body, the rest are held under Torres's WIP limit. One row changed character since this morning and should be re-read rather than re-held by habit: "Every run ends blocked on a credential only I hold" now carries a 2026-07-26 annotation disconfirming it as framed, and whether to re-frame or close it is a human's call, so ideating three solutions under its current framing would have built on a claim the tree has already retired. **Two tool refusals, both at the permission layer rather than the server.** `ost_check` was declined for the second consecutive pass, so two passes have now written to this vault without confirming its invariants afterwards; the last confirmed reading remains the fifteenth pass's 0 violations over 241 nodes, and a human should run `ost-agent check` to confirm this pass's six new nodes introduced none. `ost_flag_humans_required` was also declined, so "Time the resource questions once and count answers the vault could not already recover" could not be labelled — it needs a person by construction (the measurement is what a human says and how long they take), its body says so in prose, and a human should set the lane with `ost-agent lane`. Both refusals are appended as observed evidence on "The same agent has a different tool surface on every surface I run it on", because they refine that claim: the surface varies per-tool within a single session, not just between environments, so a partly-equipped pass is indistinguishable from a fully-equipped one until the call that fails. **Unchanged and now three passes old: the two decisions a human owes this tree** — give the gated rows a status the sweep honours (or accept `underservedOpportunities` is permanently non-empty), and build "Let a pass mark evidence acknowledged, with a reason, without inventing an opportunity" so the 41 dispositioned evidence items stop reporting unmapped forever.

passages.text: 2026-08-23 2026-08-23 unattended sweep, repo sight held: checked whether the missing instrument here is an oversight, and it is not. The mechanical half of this candidate — how many shipped helpers genuinely need a shell — is already owned by a sibling's test, "Take the harvested commands and count how many genuinely need a shell to do their work", and its harvester exists in the repo (`scripts/harvest-shell-necessity-corpus.ts`). Writing a second spec here would measure the same fact under a second name. What is left beneath this node is the one belief the harvest cannot answer: "A helper rewritten against the bundled runtime stays short enough that the operator would still edit it" — a readability judgement about a person, which no exit code settles.
